offering_description.value: Flutter offers sports and horse race betting, online casino games, poker, bingo, lotteries and daily fantasy sports to consumers. It runs betting and gaming websites and apps, operates retail sportsbooks and betting shops, and sells lottery tickets through retail networks. Its U.S. business also offers event contracts and horse racing coverage.

primary_services.value: sports and horse race betting; online casino, poker and bingo; lottery operations; daily fantasy sports contests; event contract trading

customer_segment.value: B2C: Sports and racing bettors, casino and poker players, lottery players, fantasy sports entrants and event contract traders

end_markets.value: sports and horse race wagering; online casino gaming; consumer lotteries; fantasy sports; consumer prediction markets

revenue_model.value: other: Sportsbook and casino wagers retained after paying winnings; transaction or usage fees: Commissions on betting exchanges, poker fees and paid fantasy contest entry; product sales: Flutter’s share of lottery ticket sales under operating concessions
revenue_model.category: other; transaction or usage fees; product sales

value_chain_position.value: service provider: Sets odds, takes wagers, runs games and lotteries, and settles payouts for consumers; software / platform: Uses sports data and gaming content to run consumer betting exchanges, sportsbooks and online gaming platforms

geography_served.value: global: United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Ireland, Italy, Australia, Brazil and other international markets

specialization.value: related lines: Sportsbooks, betting exchanges, casino games, poker, bingo, lotteries, fantasy sports and event contracts

distribution_channels.value: online: Betting, gaming and lottery websites and mobile apps; own locations: Company-operated betting shops and retail sportsbooks; third-party retail: Independent lottery outlets and partner venues hosting sportsbooks

regulatory_exposure.value: high: Gambling licenses and lottery concessions overseen by U.S. state regulators, the UK Gambling Commission and other national authorities.

notes: The current geographic reach of the U.S. event contract offering is uncertain.
